question.text:
$\qquad$ $\forall \, x \in \mathbb{R},\,\exists \, n \in \mathbb{N},\, x < n.$

Which of the following expresses the statement given above?
question.choice1: For every real number $x$ there is a natural number $n$ such that $x < n.$
question.choice2: For every real number $x$ there is a natural number $n$ such that $x > n.$
question.choice3: There exists a real number $x$ such that for all natural number $n,$ $x < n.$
question.choice4: There exists a real number $x$ such that for all natural number $n,$ $x > n.$
question.choice5: There exists a natural number number that is less than some real number.
question.explanation:
Our quantified statement reads as follows:

$\qquad$ For all $x \in \mathbb{R},$ there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $x < n.$

This can be re-phrased as follows:

$\qquad$ For every real number $x$ there is a natural number $n$ such that $x < n.$

question.text:
\[ \exists \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{I}}}{\,z} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, z \cdot \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{II}}}{k}\leq \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{III}}}{w}+1 \]

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
question.explanation:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\small\text{b}})$ or free $(\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\small\text{f}}).$

  • Occurrence I of the variable $z$ is bound since it's placed right next to the quantifier $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\exists}{:}$ \[ \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\exists} \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, z\cdot k \leq w+1 \]

  • Occurrence II of the variable $k$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $k.$

  • Occurrence III of the variable $w$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $w.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows: \[ \exists \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, z\cdot \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{k} \leq \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{w}+1 \]

Therefore, the free occurrences are "II and III only."

question.explanation:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\small\text{b}})$ or free $(\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\small\text{f}}).$

  • Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

  • Occurrence II of the variable $z$ is bound since it is placed right next to the quantifier $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\forall}{:}$ \[ \big( \, \exists y \in (0,1), \, {{x}y} =1 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\forall} \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} \in (1,2), \, {x} {z} > 3\, \big) \]

  • Occurrence III of the variable $z$ is bound since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $\forall{} $ that uses $z{:}$

\[ \big( \, \exists y \in (0,1), \, {{x}y} =1 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \,{\forall} {z} \in (1,2), \, \overbrace{ {x} \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} > 3 }^{\textrm{scope of $\forall z$}} \big) \]

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows: \[ \big( \, \exists \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{y} \in (0,1), \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{x} \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[3pt] \uparrow \\[4pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{y} = 1 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \forall \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} \in(1,2), \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{x}\underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} >3 \, \big) \]

Therefore, the free occurrence is "I only."

  • Occurrence III of the variable $n$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $n.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows: \[ \big( \, \exists \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{k} \in \mathbb{R}^+, \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{k} $\qquad$ \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{t} \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \forall \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{m} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{m^2} \geq \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{n} \, \big) \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers

question.text:
Let $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $y \in \mathbb{Z}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\forall \, x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+1=0.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+y=0 \, \big)$ is $\emptyset.$
  3. $\exists \, y \in \mathbb{Z}, \, \forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+y=0.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \exists \, y \in \mathbb{Z}, \, \forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+y=0 \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ There exists a integer $y$ such that, for every integer $x,$ we have $x+y=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false since $x+1=0$ is not true for some integer $x.$ Say, for $x=1.$

  • Statement II is true. The predicate \[ P(y): \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+y=0 \] is false for every value of $y.$ For example, \[ P(0): \forall \, x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x = 0 \] is false for any $x \neq 0.$ In general, it's sufficient to take $x \neq -y$ for any $y \in \mathbb{Z}.$ Therefore, its truth set is empty.

  • Statement III is false. The sentence \[ \big( \, \exists \, y \in \mathbb{Z}, \, \forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+y=0 \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \exists \, y \in \mathbb{Z} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\forall x \in \mathbb{Z}, \, x+y=0}_{P(y)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(y)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to statement II, this is not the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

example.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers

question.text:
Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\forall \, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq 10.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \, \big)$ is $\emptyset.$
  3. $\exists \, n \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \exists \, n \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ There exists a natural $n$ such that, for every natural $m,$ we have $m \leq n.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false since $m \leq 10$ is not true for some natural $m.$ Say, for $m=11.$

  • Statement II is true. The predicate \[ P(n): \quad \forall\, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \] is false for any $n\in\mathbb N.$ For example, \[ P(1) : \quad \forall\, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq 1 \] is false since $m = 2$ is not less than or equal to $1.$ Similarly, \[ P(2): \quad \forall\, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq 2 \] is false since $m = 3$ is not less than or equal to $2.$ And so on. In general, it's sufficient to take $m = n+1.$

  • Statement III is false. The sentence \[ \big( \, \exists \, n \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \exists \, n \in \mathbb{N} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\forall m \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n}_{P(n)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(n)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to statement II, this is not he case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

question.text:
Let $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y \in \mathbb{R}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{2y}\in \mathbb{R}.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{xy}\in \mathbb{R} \, \big)$ is $\mathbb{R}.$
  3. $\forall\, x,y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{xy}\in \mathbb{R}.$
question.choice1: None of the statements are true
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \forall\, x,y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{xy}\in \mathbb{R} \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ For all reals $x$ and $y,$ we have $\sqrt{xy}\in \mathbb{R}.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false since $\sqrt{2y} \in \mathbb{R}$ is not true for some real $y.$ Say, for $y=-1.$

  • Statement II is false. For the predicate \[ P(x): \quad \forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{xy} \in \mathbb{R} \] we note that $P(x)$ is false for all values $x\in\mathbb {R}.$ For example, \[ P(1) : \quad \forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{y} \in \mathbb{R} \] is false, since we can take $y=-1.$ Similarly, \[ P(2): \quad \forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{2y} \in \mathbb{R} \] is false, since we can take $y=-2.$ In general, it's sufficient to take $y=-x$ for any value of $x.$

  • Statement III is false. The sentence \[ \big( \, \forall\, x,y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{xy}\in \mathbb{R} \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \forall x \in \mathbb{R} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\forall y \in \mathbb{R}, \, \sqrt{xy} \in \mathbb{R}}_{P(x)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(x)$ is true over the universal set $\mathbb R.$ But, according to statement II, this is not the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "None of the statements are true."

question.text:
Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\forall \, n \in \mathbb{N}, \, 5 \leq n.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \, \big)$ is $\emptyset.$
  3. $\exists \, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \exists \, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ There exists a natural $m$ such that, for every natural $n,$ we have $m \leq n.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false since $5 \leq n$ is not true for some natural $n.$ Say, for $n=1.$

  • Statement II is false. The predicate \[ P(m): \quad \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \] is true for some $m\in\mathbb N.$ For example, \[ P(1) : \quad \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}, \, 1 \leq n \] is true. Therefore, its truth set is not empty.

  • Statement III is true. The sentence \[ \big( \, \exists \, m \in \mathbb{N}, \, \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \exists \, m \in \mathbb{N} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \, m \leq n}_{P(m)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(m)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to statement II, this is the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

example.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers

question.text:
Let $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y \in \mathbb{R}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\exists \, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 5y=1.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=1 \, \big)$ is $\mathbb{R}.$
  3. $\forall\, x \in \mathbb{R}, \, \exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=1.$
question.choice5: None of the statements are true
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \forall\, x \in \mathbb{R}, \, \exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=1 \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ For every real $x$ there exists real $y$ such that $xy=1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true since $5y=1$ for some real number $y$ (e.g., for $y=\dfrac{1}{5}$).

  • Statement II is false. For the predicate \[ P(x): \quad \exists \, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=1 \] we note that $P(x)$ is true for some $x\in\mathbb R$ and false for others. For example, \[ P(1): \quad \exists \, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 1\cdot y=1 \] is true since we can take $y=1.$ However, \[ P(0): \quad \exists \, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 0\cdot y=1 \] is false.

  • Statement III is false. The sentence \[ \big( \, \forall\, x \in \mathbb{R}, \, \exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=1 \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \forall\, x \in \mathbb{R} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=1}_{P(x)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(x)$ is true over the universal set $\mathbb R.$ And, according to statement II, this is not the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

example.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers
